question: After one complaint about a single report, a team changes the shared instruction, re-runs that same report, is satisfied with the result, and rolls the change out to everyone. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) The changed instruction cannot be reversed once other people begin using it
B) The person who complained will not be told the change was made for them
C) The change may fix that one report and quietly damage every other kind
D) Re-running one report will consume more of the team's allowance than usual
correct_answers: C) The change may fix that one report and quietly damage every other kind
explanations: Instructions can be changed back at any time, so reversibility is not the exposure here.
Failing to close the loop with the complainant is a courtesy issue, not the reason the rollout is unsafe.

Correct. Testing a fix only on the case that failed shows that the case now passes; it says nothing about the reports that were already fine. Trying it on a few different real cases is what would reveal the damage.
The cost of re-running one report is trivial and unrelated to whether the change was sound.
